architecture.mechanism: Coupled transmission ratio-efficiency modeling that integrates a refined multi-source loss model (meshing, bearing, churning, and windage losses) with kinematic/topological analysis, optimized via multi-objective particle swarm optimization to identify high-efficiency operating zones and tune structural and lubrication parameters, yielding stable thermal and dynamic behavior.
architecture.intervention: Apply the unified ratio-efficiency coupled modeling framework to the failed vehicle's multi-speed gearbox: build a topological kinematic model, calibrate the multi-source loss model against bench tests under the vehicle's load spectrum, then use the enhanced MOPSO algorithm to redesign the gear ratios and lubrication parameters so that the transmission's everyday operating points (cruise, light-load acceleration) fall within the computed high-efficiency zone, reducing meshing/bearing/churning/windage losses and heat generation that would otherwise degrade clutch packs, bands, and synchronizers.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced mechanical and thermal losses in the transmission, keeping operating temperatures and torque fluctuations within design limits, which mitigates premature wear that produces hard shifting and slipping and extends reliable service life of the gearbox well beyond the 460-mile failure point.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the redesigned transmission on a bench dynamometer following the paper's protocol (efficiency MAP measurements, thermal endurance tests, and dynamic response evaluations) under the same duty cycle that produced the in-vehicle failure; the redesign is falsified if peak oil temperature still rises above the original spec during the endurance test, if measured efficiency MAP does not shift operating points into the predicted high-efficiency zone, or if hard-shift/slip symptoms recur in a follow-up NHTSA-complaint recheck on the optimized vehicle.
